legend: You are given a sequence of positive integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%%.
A pair of integers x,y%%ZSMJ2%% is good if max(x,y)<x⊕y%%ZSMJ3%%, where ⊕%%ZSMJ4%% denotes the bitwise XOR operation.
A set S%%ZSMJ5%% of integers counts if all its elements are unique, and all pairs of distinct integers in S%%ZSMJ6%% are good.
What is the largest subset of a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ7%% that counts?
input: The second line contains n%%ZSMJ10%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ11%% (1≤ai≤4⋅106%%ZSMJ12%%).
output: Print the size of the largest subset of a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ13%% that counts.
note: In the first test, the set {1,2}%%ZSMJ14%% counts, since 1⊕2=3%%ZSMJ15%%, while max(1,2)=2%%ZSMJ16%%, and 3>2%%ZSMJ17%%. However, {1,2,3}%%ZSMJ18%% does not count, since, for example, 1⊕3=2≤max(1,3)=3%%ZSMJ19%%. So the answer is 2%%ZSMJ20%%.
In the second test, the optimal solution is to just take the set {4000000}%%ZSMJ21%%.
